explainer.summary: WETH9 is an ERC20-compatible wrapper for Ether on Ethereum, allowing ETH to be deposited and represented as WETH tokens that can be transferred or approved like standard tokens. The contract accepts ETH via fallback or deposit, credits balances, and allows withdrawal of equivalent ETH. It uses Solidity 0.4.18 with no owner, admin controls, or upgrade mechanisms present in the source.

key_functions.name: deposit
key_functions.what: Accepts payable ETH and increases msg.sender's balanceOf by msg.value while emitting Deposit.

key_functions.name: withdraw
key_functions.what: Requires sufficient balanceOf[msg.sender], subtracts wad, transfers ETH via msg.sender.transfer, and emits Withdrawal.

key_functions.name: totalSupply
key_functions.what: Returns the contract's ETH balance (this.balance) as the total WETH supply.

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: Sets allowance[msg.sender][guy] = wad and emits Approval.

key_functions.name: transfer
key_functions.what: Delegates to transferFrom(msg.sender, dst, wad).

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Checks balanceOf[src] >= wad, deducts from allowance if src != msg.sender and allowance != uint(-1), updates balances, emits Transfer.

key_functions.name: fallback
key_functions.what: Payable function that unconditionally calls deposit().

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; the contract has no proxy, owner, or selfdestruct logic and is immutable as deployed.
user_risks: Allowance value of uint(-1) is treated as infinite and never decremented on transfers.
withdraw performs an external ETH transfer after state update but relies on 0.4.x transfer semantics.
No built-in reentrancy guard; callers must ensure safe usage patterns around ETH transfers.
integration_tips: Call deposit() or send ETH directly to wrap; use withdraw(uint) to unwrap.
Check allowance[src][msg.sender] != uint(-1) before assuming standard deduction in custom logic.
totalSupply reflects actual contract ETH balance, not a stored variable.
Use transferFrom for allowance-based moves; approve sets exact values with no increase/decrease helpers.

explainer.summary: TetherToken is an ERC20 token extending Pausable, StandardToken and BlackList, with initial supply assigned to owner and optional fee logic in transfers. It supports a deprecation flag that forwards calls to an upgraded contract address set by owner. All statements derive directly from the provided TetherToken.sol source.

key_functions.name: transfer
key_functions.what: Transfers tokens applying optional fee to owner if basisPointsRate > 0, reverts if paused or sender blacklisted, forwards to upgraded contract if deprecated.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Transfers from allowance applying optional fee, reverts if paused or from blacklisted, forwards if deprecated.

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: Sets allowance after checking for zero race condition, forwards if deprecated.

key_functions.name: balanceOf
key_functions.what: Returns balance, forwards to upgraded contract if deprecated.

key_functions.name: totalSupply
key_functions.what: Returns _totalSupply, forwards to upgraded contract if deprecated.

key_functions.name: addBlackList
key_functions.what: Owner-only function that sets isBlackListed[_evilUser] = true.

key_functions.name: destroyBlackFunds
key_functions.what: Owner-only function that zeros balance of blacklisted address and subtracts from _totalSupply.

key_functions.name: issue
key_functions.what: Owner-only function that increases _totalSupply and owner balance.

key_functions.name: redeem
key_functions.what: Owner-only function that decreases _totalSupply and owner balance.

key_functions.name: deprecate
key_functions.what: Owner-only function that sets deprecated=true and upgradedAddress.

admin_powers: pause and unpause transfers via onlyOwner whenNotPaused/whenPaused
addBlackList, removeBlackList and destroyBlackFunds on any address
issue and redeem tokens affecting _totalSupply and owner balance
setParams for basisPointsRate (<20) and maximumFee (<50)
transferOwnership and deprecate to new upgradedAddress
call transfer/transferFrom/approve on behalf of blacklisted users is blocked but owner can still manage lists
explainer.upgradeability: Boolean deprecated flag plus upgradedAddress; when true, transfer/transferFrom/balanceOf/approve/allowance/totalSupply delegate to UpgradedStandardToken at upgradedAddress via transferByLegacy etc.
user_risks: owner can pause all transfers
owner can blacklist any address and destroy its funds reducing totalSupply
owner can issue arbitrary new tokens to self
possible transfer fees up to maximumFee if setParams called
contract can be deprecated rendering current instance a proxy
integration_tips: always call totalSupply/balanceOf through the current TetherToken address as it may delegate
check deprecated flag before assuming direct storage values
transfers may deduct fee sent to owner; use onlyPayloadSize-safe calls
allowance approvals must first set to zero if changing non-zero value

explainer.summary: FiatTokenV2_2 extends FiatTokenV2_1 and adds initializeV2_2 to migrate deprecated blacklists, update the symbol, and set _initializedVersion to 3. It overrides blacklist and balance storage using the high bit of balanceAndBlacklistStates for the blacklist flag while keeping balances in the lower 255 bits. Signed permit and authorization functions delegate to internal _ methods, and _domainSeparator uses EIP712 version "2" with the current chainId.

key_functions.name: initializeV2_2
key_functions.what: Requires _initializedVersion == 2, sets symbol, migrates accounts from _deprecatedBlacklisted to _blacklist, blacklists the contract itself, and sets _initializedVersion = 3.

key_functions.name: permit
key_functions.what: External whenNotPaused wrapper that calls _permit with a bytes signature.

key_functions.name: transferWithAuthorization
key_functions.what: External whenNotPaused notBlacklisted wrapper that calls _transferWithAuthorization.

key_functions.name: receiveWithAuthorization
key_functions.what: External whenNotPaused notBlacklisted wrapper that calls _receiveWithAuthorization and checks payee matches caller.

key_functions.name: cancelAuthorization
key_functions.what: External whenNotPaused wrapper that calls _cancelAuthorization.

key_functions.name: _setBlacklistState
key_functions.what: Sets high bit of balanceAndBlacklistStates via OR or resets to _balanceOf depending on _shouldBlacklist.

key_functions.name: _setBalance
key_functions.what: Requires balance <= (2^255-1) and not blacklisted, then stores value in balanceAndBlacklistStates.

key_functions.name: _isBlacklisted
key_functions.what: Returns true if high bit of balanceAndBlacklistStates is 1.

key_functions.name: _balanceOf
key_functions.what: Returns lower 255 bits of balanceAndBlacklistStates via AND mask.

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: External whenNotPaused override that calls _approve.

explainer.upgradeability: initializeV2_2 must be called exactly once when _initializedVersion == 2; it permanently sets version to 3 and performs one-time blacklist migration.
user_risks: Accounts can be blacklisted, freezing their balances and preventing transfers or approvals.
Balances cannot exceed (2^255 - 1) or the transaction reverts.
Signed authorizations and permits can be front-run or replayed if nonces and deadlines are mishandled.
integration_tips: Call initializeV2_2 with the exact list of accounts that were blacklisted under the deprecated mapping.
Use the bytes-signature permit and authorization overloads for EOA wallets (r,s,v packed).
Query balances and blacklist status via the overridden _balanceOf and _isBlacklisted logic rather than direct storage reads.

explainer.summary: Dai is an ERC20 token with auth-controlled minting and EIP-2612-style permit support via DOMAIN_SEPARATOR and PERMIT_TYPEHASH. It inherits LibNote for note logging on auth and token functions, uses wards mapping for access control, and implements transferFrom/burn with infinite allowance optimization.

key_functions.name: rely
key_functions.what: Grants ward status to an address, callable only by auth.

key_functions.name: deny
key_functions.what: Revokes ward status from an address, callable only by auth.

key_functions.name: mint
key_functions.what: Increases balance and totalSupply for a user, callable only by auth.

key_functions.name: burn
key_functions.what: Decreases balance and totalSupply after allowance check if not self.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Moves tokens with balance and allowance checks, skipping allowance update on infinite allowance.

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: Sets allowance and emits Approval event.

key_functions.name: permit
key_functions.what: Sets allowance via EIP-712 signature after nonce, expiry, and ecrecover validation.

key_functions.name: push
key_functions.what: Alias for transferFrom from msg.sender.

key_functions.name: pull
key_functions.what: Alias for transferFrom to msg.sender.

key_functions.name: move
key_functions.what: Alias for transferFrom between arbitrary addresses.

admin_powers: Add/remove authorized addresses that can call mint via rely/deny
explainer.upgradeability: No upgradeability; contract is immutable with no delegatecall or proxy logic present in source.
user_risks: Any ward can mint arbitrary amounts increasing totalSupply
permit requires correct DOMAIN_SEPARATOR computed at deployment with chainId
integration_tips: Check for allowance == uint(-1) to avoid unnecessary storage writes on transfers
Use permit with allowed=true to set infinite allowance via signature
nonces must be tracked off-chain and incremented exactly once per successful permit

explainer.summary: UniswapV2Factory (constructor takes _feeToSetter) deploys UniswapV2Pair instances via CREATE2 in createPair after validating distinct non-zero tokens and checking getPair[token0][token1] == address(0). It exposes getPair, allPairs, allPairsLength, feeTo and feeToSetter; only feeToSetter may call setFeeTo or setFeeToSetter. The factory stores no upgrade logic and the Pair contracts it creates contain the full mint/burn/swap logic shown in the source.

key_functions.name: createPair
key_functions.what: validates tokens, deploys UniswapV2Pair with CREATE2 using salt from token0/token1, calls initialize, records in getPair and allPairs, emits PairCreated

key_functions.name: setFeeTo
key_functions.what: sets feeTo only if msg.sender == feeToSetter

key_functions.name: setFeeToSetter
key_functions.what: sets feeToSetter only if msg.sender == feeToSetter

key_functions.name: getPair
key_functions.what: public mapping returning the pair address for token0/token1

key_functions.name: allPairs
key_functions.what: public array of all created pair addresses

key_functions.name: allPairsLength
key_functions.what: returns allPairs.length

key_functions.name: feeTo
key_functions.what: public address receiving protocol fees when enabled

key_functions.name: feeToSetter
key_functions.what: public address authorized to change feeTo and itself

admin_powers: feeToSetter may call setFeeTo to change the fee recipient
feeToSetter may call setFeeToSetter to transfer admin rights
explainer.upgradeability: None; constructor sets immutable feeToSetter and no proxy or delegatecall patterns exist in the source.
user_risks: feeToSetter is a single trusted address that can redirect protocol fees
createPair will revert if tokens are identical, zero, or a pair already exists
Pair contracts enforce reentrancy lock and K invariant but rely on correct token balances
integration_tips: Call createPair only from contracts that have performed token sorting and existence checks
Read getPair[token0][token1] before createPair to avoid the PAIR_EXISTS revert
Use allPairsLength and allPairs to enumerate pairs; feeTo must be monitored separately via events

explainer.summary: This contract is UniswapV2Router02 (implements IUniswapV2Router02) with immutable factory and WETH addresses set in the constructor. It provides liquidity addition/removal and token/ETH swaps (including fee-on-transfer variants) via internal calls to UniswapV2Library and IUniswapV2Pair, all guarded by the ensure(deadline) modifier. No owner or admin state exists in the provided source.

key_functions.name: addLiquidity
key_functions.what: calls _addLiquidity then transfers tokens to pair and mints liquidity

key_functions.name: addLiquidityETH
key_functions.what: adds ETH liquidity by depositing to WETH and minting pair liquidity

key_functions.name: removeLiquidity
key_functions.what: transfers LP to pair then burns and returns sorted token amounts

key_functions.name: swapExactTokensForTokens
key_functions.what: computes amounts via getAmountsOut, transfers input, then calls _swap

key_functions.name: swapExactETHForTokens
key_functions.what: deposits msg.value to WETH then performs swap if path starts with WETH

key_functions.name: _swap
key_functions.what: iterates path, computes token0-based out amounts, and calls pair.swap

key_functions.name: _swapSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens
key_functions.what: computes actual input from pair balance delta then swaps

key_functions.name: quote
key_functions.what: delegates to UniswapV2Library.quote

key_functions.name: getAmountsOut
key_functions.what: delegates to UniswapV2Library.getAmountsOut

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; factory and WETH are immutable and set only in constructor.
user_risks: deadline must be >= block.timestamp or transaction reverts
amountOutMin / amountAMin checks can fail on slippage
fee-on-transfer tokens require the Supporting variants
integration_tips: always pass a future deadline and sufficient min amounts
use getAmountsOut / getAmountsIn for pre-flight quotes
for ETH use the WETH-wrapped variants

explainer.summary: The SwapRouter contract provides stateless execution of exact-input and exact-output swaps against Uniswap V3 pools via single-hop and multi-hop paths encoded in bytes. It inherits PeripheryImmutableState (set once in the constructor with factory and WETH9), PeripheryValidation (deadline checks), PeripheryPaymentsWithFee, Multicall, and SelfPermit. All swap logic routes through uniswapV3SwapCallback and internal helpers that call pool.swap and pay tokens.

key_functions.name: exactInputSingle
key_functions.what: Performs a single-hop exact-input swap with amountOutMinimum and deadline check.

key_functions.name: exactInput
key_functions.what: Performs a multi-hop exact-input swap by iterating the path and using intermediate custody at the router.

key_functions.name: exactOutputSingle
key_functions.what: Performs a single-hop exact-output swap with amountInMaximum and resets amountInCached.

key_functions.name: exactOutput
key_functions.what: Performs a multi-hop exact-output swap and reads the final amountIn from amountInCached.

key_functions.name: multicall
key_functions.what: Executes multiple encoded calls via delegatecall and reverts with decoded error strings on failure.

key_functions.name: selfPermit
key_functions.what: Calls permit on an ERC20Permit token to approve the router.

key_functions.name: uniswapV3SwapCallback
key_functions.what: Validates the callback, decodes the path, and pays the required tokenIn to the pool.

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; state is immutable after constructor sets factory and WETH9.
user_risks: Transaction reverts if block.timestamp exceeds deadline
Swaps revert if amountOut < amountOutMinimum or amountIn > amountInMaximum
amountInCached is transient and must be reset after exactOutputSingle
integration_tips: Batch approvals and swaps in a single multicall using selfPermit* functions
Set recipient to address(0) to custody intermediate tokens at the router
Use Path library helpers to build and traverse multi-pool paths

explainer.summary: Permit2 inherits from SignatureTransfer and AllowanceTransfer to support both signature-based token transfers and stored allowance transfers in one contract. It uses EIP712 with cached domain separator and chainId for replay protection across forks. All transfer functions require prior token approval to Permit2 as stated in the contract comment.

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: Sets amount and expiration in allowance mapping for a token and spender.

key_functions.name: permit
key_functions.what: Verifies signature and updates approval from PermitSingle or PermitBatch.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Transfers using stored allowance, checking expiration and amount.

key_functions.name: lockdown
key_functions.what: Sets allowance amount to zero for listed token-spender pairs.

key_functions.name: invalidateNonces
key_functions.what: Updates nonce in PackedAllowance after validating newNonce > oldNonce.

key_functions.name: permitTransferFrom
key_functions.what: Verifies signature, uses unordered nonce, and transfers permitted token amount.

key_functions.name: permitWitnessTransferFrom
key_functions.what: Same as permitTransferFrom but includes witness hash for additional data.

key_functions.name: invalidateUnorderedNonces
key_functions.what: Sets bits in nonceBitmap to invalidate nonces.

key_functions.name: DOMAIN_SEPARATOR
key_functions.what: Returns cached or rebuilt EIP712 domain separator based on current chainId.

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; the contract has no proxy or owner-controlled upgrade logic and deploys as immutable bytecode.
user_risks: SignatureExpired if block.timestamp exceeds sigDeadline or deadline in permit structs.
InvalidNonce if signed nonce does not match stored nonce or if nonce bit already set.
AllowanceExpired or InsufficientAllowance during _transfer if expiration passed or amount exceeded.
Users must call token approve on Permit2 before any transferFrom or permitTransferFrom succeeds.
integration_tips: Call ERC20 approve on the token for Permit2 address before using allowance or signature transfers.
Use DOMAIN_SEPARATOR for off-chain signature generation to ensure correct EIP712 hashing.
Batch functions accept arrays but enforce length match between permitted and transferDetails.
nonceBitmap and allowance mappings are public for on-chain or off-chain nonce tracking.

explainer.summary: The Uni contract implements the UNI governance token as an ERC-20 with 18 decimals and 1B total supply. It adds delegation-based voting checkpoints, EIP-2612 permits, and a single minter address that may mint at most 2% of supply once per year after mintingAllowedAfter. All arithmetic uses SafeMath; balances and allowances are stored as uint96.

key_functions.name: mint
key_functions.what: Callable only by minter after mintingAllowedAfter; mints up to mintCap percent of totalSupply and advances the next mint timestamp by one year.

key_functions.name: setMinter
key_functions.what: Allows the current minter to transfer minting rights to a new address.

key_functions.name: delegate
key_functions.what: Transfers the caller's voting power to the given delegatee and records the change via checkpoints.

key_functions.name: delegateBySig
key_functions.what: Delegates votes using an EIP-712 signature, consuming a nonce and checking expiry.

key_functions.name: getPriorVotes
key_functions.what: Returns the vote balance of an account at a specific past block number using binary search over checkpoints.

key_functions.name: permit
key_functions.what: Sets allowance via EIP-712 signature with deadline and nonce, avoiding a separate approve transaction.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Moves tokens while decreasing the spender's allowance unless it is set to uint96(-1).

key_functions.name: balanceOf
key_functions.what: Returns the uint96 balance stored for an account.

admin_powers: setMinter (only current minter)
mint (only current minter, subject to time and cap)
explainer.upgradeability: None; the contract has no proxy, owner, or upgrade mechanism and is deployed as a plain contract at the verified address.
user_risks: The designated minter can mint up to 2% of totalSupply once per year.
Approvals are overwritten by approve and are subject to the known ERC-20 race condition described in the code comment.
Vote delegation and checkpoints rely on correct block numbers; getPriorVotes reverts for unfinalized blocks.
integration_tips: Use balanceOf/transfer/approve for standard ERC-20 interactions; all amounts must fit in 96 bits.
Track voting power via getCurrentVotes or getPriorVotes rather than raw balances when integrating with governance.
Call delegate or delegateBySig immediately after receiving tokens if the recipient should vote with them.
Permit signatures must match the exact DOMAIN_TYPEHASH and PERMIT_TYPEHASH defined in the contract.

explainer.summary: LinkToken is a fixed-supply ERC20 token (totalSupply=10**27) that also implements ERC677 via ERC677Token. All tokens are assigned to the deployer in the constructor; the contract contains no mint, burn, ownership or admin functions. Transfers, approvals and transferAndCall are guarded by the validRecipient modifier that rejects the zero address and the token contract itself.

key_functions.name: transfer
key_functions.what: Moves tokens from msg.sender to _to after subtracting from sender and adding to recipient; emits Transfer.

key_functions.name: transferFrom
key_functions.what: Moves tokens from _from to _to using allowance, updates balances and allowance, emits Transfer.

key_functions.name: approve
key_functions.what: Sets allowed[msg.sender][_spender] = _value and emits Approval.

key_functions.name: increaseApproval
key_functions.what: Adds _addedValue to the current allowance and emits Approval with the new value.

key_functions.name: decreaseApproval
key_functions.what: Subtracts _subtractedValue from allowance (or sets to 0 if larger) and emits Approval.

key_functions.name: transferAndCall
key_functions.what: Calls super.transfer then Transfer with data; if _to is a contract, invokes onTokenTransfer on it.

key_functions.name: balanceOf
key_functions.what: Returns the recorded balance for the given address from the balances mapping.

key_functions.name: allowance
key_functions.what: Returns the remaining allowance from owner to spender stored in the allowed mapping.

explainer.upgradeability: None. The contract is a plain, non-upgradeable deployment with no proxy, owner or delegatecall mechanisms.
user_risks: approve race-condition still possible if callers do not use increaseApproval/decreaseApproval.
transferAndCall silently succeeds even if the recipient contract's onTokenTransfer reverts (no try/catch).
All tokens are minted to the single deployer address; no further supply control exists.
integration_tips: Call increaseApproval/decreaseApproval instead of approve when the allowance may already be non-zero.
When receiving LINK via transferAndCall, implement ERC677Receiver.onTokenTransfer to handle the data payload.
Use validRecipient semantics: the token will revert on transfers to address(0) or to itself.

explainer.summary: GnosisSafe v1.3.0 is a multisig wallet singleton (contracts/GnosisSafe.sol) that can only be used via proxies because its constructor sets threshold=1 and prevents further setup. It inherits EtherPaymentFallback, Singleton, ModuleManager, OwnerManager, FallbackManager, GuardManager and others; initialization occurs once via setup() which calls setupOwners, internalSetFallbackHandler and setupModules. All subsequent execution flows through execTransaction which encodes a SafeTx, increments nonce, checks signatures via checkNSignatures, optionally runs a guard, then calls Executor.execute.

key_functions.name: setup
key_functions.what: Initializes owners, threshold, fallbackHandler, modules and optional payment; reverts if already initialized because setupOwners checks threshold.

key_functions.name: execTransaction
key_functions.what: Encodes transaction data, increments nonce, verifies signatures with checkSignatures, runs guard checks, executes via Executor.execute and handles gas payment.

key_functions.name: checkNSignatures
key_functions.what: Validates exactly requiredSignatures ECDSA, approved-hash (v=1) or contract (v=0) signatures against owners mapping and EIP-1271.

key_functions.name: encodeTransactionData
key_functions.what: Builds the EIP-712 SafeTx hash using SAFE_TX_TYPEHASH, domainSeparator and all transaction fields including nonce.

key_functions.name: approveHash
key_functions.what: Marks a hash in approvedHashes[msg.sender] so it can be used with v=1 signatures.

key_functions.name: setGuard
key_functions.what: Authorized-only setter that stores guard address in GUARD_STORAGE_SLOT.

key_functions.name: setFallbackHandler
key_functions.what: Authorized-only setter that stores handler in FALLBACK_HANDLER_STORAGE_SLOT; fallback delegate-calls it.

key_functions.name: handlePayment
key_functions.what: Transfers gasUsed+baseGas * gasPrice in ETH or ERC20 to refundReceiver or tx.origin.

admin_powers: setupOwners and setupModules (only callable once via setup)
setGuard and setFallbackHandler via authorized modifier (self-call only)
addOwnerWithThreshold, removeOwner, swapOwner, changeThreshold from OwnerManager (not shown but imported)
explainer.upgradeability: Singleton contract deployed at 0xd9Db270c1B5E3Bd161E8c8503c55cEABeE709552; proxies delegatecall to it; no on-chain upgrade logic present in the provided source.
user_risks: Threshold=0 or owner=0 checks in checkNSignatures can brick the Safe
DelegateCall operation allows arbitrary code execution if owners approve it
Guard or fallbackHandler can be set to malicious contracts via Safe transaction
Payment can be forced even on failed transactions when gasPrice>0
integration_tips: Always call setup exactly once through the proxy constructor initializer
Use getTransactionHash to obtain the EIP-712 hash that owners must sign
Provide at least safeTxGas+2500+500 gas when calling execTransaction
Check that guard returns without revert in both checkTransaction and checkAfterExecution

explainer.summary: Multicall3 aggregates multiple external calls in one transaction via structs Call, Call3, and Call3Value, returning block data and per-call Result structs; variants like aggregate require success while tryAggregate and aggregate3 support per-call allowFailure. It includes view helpers for block.number, blockhash, coinbase, difficulty, gaslimit, timestamp, basefee, chainid, and address balances. The contract has no owner, admin, or state-mutating functions beyond the call aggregation logic itself.

key_functions.name: aggregate
key_functions.what: Executes Call[] requiring every call to succeed, returns blockNumber and returnData[]

key_functions.name: tryAggregate
key_functions.what: Executes Call[] with optional requireSuccess flag, returns Result[]

key_functions.name: tryBlockAndAggregate
key_functions.what: Calls tryAggregate and also returns blockNumber and blockHash

key_functions.name: blockAndAggregate
key_functions.what: Calls tryBlockAndAggregate with requireSuccess=true

key_functions.name: aggregate3
key_functions.what: Executes Call3[] allowing per-call allowFailure, reverts on failure when not allowed

key_functions.name: aggregate3Value
key_functions.what: Executes Call3Value[] sending per-call value, checks msg.value equals sum of values

key_functions.name: getBlockHash
key_functions.what: Returns blockhash(blockNumber)

key_functions.name: getEthBalance
key_functions.what: Returns addr.balance

key_functions.name: getChainId
key_functions.what: Returns block.chainid

explainer.upgradeability: Not upgradeable; the contract contains no proxy, owner, or upgrade logic and all functions are implemented directly in the deployed bytecode.
user_risks: aggregate and blockAndAggregate revert the entire transaction if any call fails
aggregate3Value reverts if msg.value does not equal the sum of call values
External calls execute with the multicall contract as msg.sender
integration_tips: Prefer aggregate3 or aggregate3Value for new integrations to support selective failure handling
Marking aggregate methods payable saves gas per the contract comment
Use the view helpers instead of direct opcodes for consistent cross-chain behavior

explainer.summary: ENSRegistryWithFallback extends ENSRegistry and adds fallback reads to a prior ENS instance stored in the immutable 'old' field. Records are stored only in the new mapping; resolver/owner/ttl fall back to old when !recordExists(node). _setOwner maps a zero owner to address(this) before writing.

key_functions.name: constructor
key_functions.what: Calls ENSRegistry() then stores the supplied ENS _old contract.

key_functions.name: resolver
key_functions.what: Returns super.resolver(node) if recordExists(node), else old.resolver(node).

key_functions.name: owner
key_functions.what: Returns super.owner(node) if recordExists(node), else old.owner(node); zero address is returned as 0x0.

key_functions.name: ttl
key_functions.what: Returns super.ttl(node) if recordExists(node), else old.ttl(node).

key_functions.name: setOwner
key_functions.what: Authorised modifier check then _setOwner which stores address(this) for a zero owner.

key_functions.name: setSubnodeOwner
key_functions.what: Authorised check, computes subnode hash, calls _setOwner and emits NewOwner.

key_functions.name: setApprovalForAll
key_functions.what: Sets operators[msg.sender][operator] and emits ApprovalForAll.

key_functions.name: recordExists
key_functions.what: True when records[node].owner != address(0x0).

admin_powers: Initial msg.sender becomes owner of the root node 0x0 in ENSRegistry constructor
explainer.upgradeability: No proxy or upgrade mechanism; migration occurs via read-only fallback to the immutable 'old' ENS contract.
user_risks: Zero owner address is rewritten to address(this) inside _setOwner
Reads silently return values from the old registry until a record is created in the new one
integration_tips: Call recordExists before trusting owner/resolver/ttl results
Use setRecord or setSubnodeRecord to populate new storage and stop fallback

explainer.summary: Seaport 1.5 (contracts/Seaport.sol) inherits from Consideration and implements a marketplace for native/ERC20/ERC721/ERC1155 orders via offer/consideration items. The provided source shows only the constructor (passing conduitController) plus internal overrides _name and _nameString; all transfer logic resides in the inherited Executor contract.

key_functions.name: constructor
key_functions.what: Takes conduitController address and passes it to Consideration base constructor.

key_functions.name: _name
key_functions.what: Internal pure override returning contract name via assembly ("Seaport").

key_functions.name: _nameString
key_functions.what: Internal pure override returning the string "Seaport" for name hash derivation.

key_functions.name: _transfer
key_functions.what: Internal function dispatching to native/ERC20/ERC721/ERC1155 transfer paths based on ItemType.

key_functions.name: _transferNativeTokens
key_functions.what: Internal function performing native token call, reverting with NativeTokenTransferGenericFailure on failure.

key_functions.name: _transferERC20
key_functions.what: Internal function routing ERC20 transfers directly or via conduit accumulator.

explainer.summary: This contract implements the CryptoPunks NFT marketplace with 10000 punks initially assigned by the owner via setInitialOwner and setInitialOwners before allInitialOwnersAssigned locks further assignment. After that, ownership is tracked in punkIndexToAddress and balanceOf, with on-chain offers in punksOfferedForSale and bids in punkBids, using pendingWithdrawals for payments. All state-changing functions after assignment require allPunksAssigned to be true and enforce sender ownership checks.

key_functions.what: Constructor sets owner, totalSupply=10000, punksRemainingToAssign, name, symbol and decimals.

key_functions.name: transferPunk
key_functions.what: Transfers punk ownership, cancels any active offer, and refunds a bid if the recipient is the bidder.

key_functions.what: Lists a punk for sale at minSalePriceInWei to anyone.

key_functions.name: buyPunk
key_functions.what: Purchases an offered punk if msg.value meets minValue and seller still owns it, crediting seller via pendingWithdrawals.

key_functions.what: Submits a bid higher than any existing bid, refunding the prior bidder via pendingWithdrawals.

key_functions.name: acceptBidForPunk
key_functions.what: Seller accepts the current bid if it meets minPrice, transferring ownership and crediting via pendingWithdrawals.

key_functions.name: withdraw
key_functions.what: Sends the caller's pendingWithdrawals amount after zeroing the balance to prevent re-entrancy.
